name: soft chipped bites of dirt in the north-west, south-west corners of one old asphalt road tile, rounding off the inside corners where roads meet at a junction: irregular quarter-blobs of dirt about 4 px across with broken lighter asphalt edges (or dry dark ledges on their south sides), loose asphalt crumbs on the dirt and dirt flecks on the road; transparent elsewhere, shown on a real T junction or crossing
label: wasteland_ruins/asphalt-in-nw-sw

refSet.reason: 칩셋 wasteland_ruins 의 화풍 기준 묶음이 없다

surfaces.part: dirt ground patch with a gray asphalt cross-shaped road strip

answer.evidence: The image is a flat top-down view of a full 112x112 opaque dirt field with a gray asphalt cross or T-shaped road on it, rows 18-92 for the vertical arm and rows 49-62 for the horizontal arm. There is no front face and no eave or edge-line structure. The only dark 1-3 row strips, such as rows 60-62 under the left arm, are small ledge shadows on the asphalt, not a vertical south face. The scan shows mottled dirt tones (#7b5d48, #916f57) and asphalt tones (#524b49, #7b7270) with no ellipse and no roof. It reads as a flat ground decal, which fits the 'flat' kind. It does not match the description of transparent surroundings with small corner bites.

styleAnswer.evidence: The dirt carries mottled speckle in about 4 brown tones, so it reads as textured and matches the grass reference (3 visible tones, 0% flat). The asphalt strips of the T junction are weaker. They show roughly 3 tones: a mid grey body, a lighter chipped edge and a few dark flecks. Their interiors are fairly smooth, with no per-tile grain or crumb clusters, and the shapes are blocky. There is no neutral black sticker outline (0% near-neutral dark edge pixels), and edges are separated by value, which suits the Beodeul approach. However, the dirt-to-asphalt transition has no distinct broken lighter edges or dark south ledges, and the loose crumbs and flecks are sparse. On the primary facts (5 visible tones, 1% near-flat) the piece sits above the grass reference and below the paving reference (7 tones). Overall the shading is shallower than Beodeul's 5-6 steps per material, so I am calling it slightly lower and failing it on the benefit of the doubt.

surfaces.part: dirt ground tile with asphalt road T junction, drawn flat from above
dark ledge under the west road arm

answer.evidence: The whole 112x112 tile is a flat top-down ground texture. The dirt fills every row (width 112 from row 0 to 111), and the gray asphalt road forms a T/cross shape on it. There is no vertical front face. The only vertical hint is a 1-2 row dark ledge under the west arm at about rows 61-63, which is a rim and not a face of 3+ rows. The column scans show only alternating dirt and asphalt textures with no edge-line-plus-eave structure. This is a flat decal read from above, so it is a top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has only 9 distinct colours in total, against 80 for the grass and 7 per tile for the paving. It shows 5 visible tones per tile, which is above the grass (3) but below the paving (7). The dirt is a mottled brown with only about 3 to 4 steps. The grey asphalt strips are nearly flat, with perhaps 2 to 3 steps and no per-tile highlights, crumbs or grain, so they read as pasted-on shapes. There are no real outlines. Edges are separated by value alone, which is fine, but the broken lighter asphalt edges and dry dark ledges described for the dirt bites are barely visible. Dirt speckle keeps near-flat coverage at 1%, so there are no big flat fills. The ramps are still clearly shallower than the 5-6 steps per material in Beodeul, and the candidate looks thinner than the paving reference, so it fails.

surfaces.part: dirt ground with asphalt road strips (T junction or crossing) seen from above

answer.evidence: The whole 112x112 image is a flat top-down ground texture: mottled dirt with grey asphalt road strips running vertically (about rows 15-91) and horizontally (about rows 39-62). The width is 112 on every row. The column scans show only mottled dirt and asphalt colour runs, with no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no vertical face. The few dark ledge rows, such as rows 62-63 under the west arm and the 1-row shadows at the bottoms of the bites, are thin edge details rather than a front face of 3 or more rows. This is a flat decal with no front face, which suits the flat kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a brown dirt field with a thin grey asphalt T shape. The dirt has speckle and blotches, so it is not flat: near-flat coverage is 1% and there are 5 visible tones per tile. That is above the grass reference (3) but below the paving reference (7). Only 9 distinct colours are used in total. The dirt reads as about 3 steps (base, dark blotch, light fleck) and the asphalt as about 2-3 (mid grey, darker grey, a faint lighter edge). The references carry 5-6 steps per material, with per-stone highlights on the paving and clumps on the grass. The asphalt strip is a nearly uniform grey with little grain, no per-tile or crumb highlights and no clear broken lighter edge. The dirt bites are small and hard to read at the corners of the road. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so there is no black sticker outline, and forms separate mostly by value, but the shading ramps are shallow. The piece sits below the reference in shading depth and asphalt texture richness, and with doubt resolving to fail, it fails.

surfaces.part: dirt ground tile with asphalt road junction

answer.evidence: The whole 112x112 image is one flat, fully opaque plate. It shows a mottled dirt field with a grey asphalt road in a T or cross shape, viewed straight down. The road columns (x=56 rows 18-91, plus the west arm at rows ~50-61) are flat grey with lighter and darker speckle. The only dark lines are thin 1-2 row ledges under the west arm (rows 61-62) and at the bottom of the south arm (about row 92). These are shading on the flat decal, not a vertical front face of 3 or more rows. There is no ellipse, roof or eave, and no object volume. It is a flat decal, so there is no front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a dirt field with a grey asphalt T-shape, so the tile is mostly dirt. The dirt has only about 3-4 close brown tones scattered as even speckle, not clustered into crumbs, clods or grain clumps. The asphalt reads as roughly 2-3 grey steps with a light edge and a dark ledge. That is well short of the 5-6 steps per material in the Beodeul references. Only 9 distinct colours exist across the whole piece. The measured facts are 5 visible tones per tile, which is above the grass reference (3) but below the paving reference (7). Near-flat coverage is 1%, so there are no big flat fills. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted rather than a black sticker line. The 4px dirt bites and the asphalt crumbs are barely distinguishable at this scale, and the asphalt has no per-tile highlights or stone-by-stone shading like the paving reference. The result is competent but shallower than the standard, and when in doubt it fails.
